answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by putting a bonded identity kernel at the center of earning. Every new account must lock a deposit for several epochs before its answers settle, so cheap replicas do not pay. Peer graders then paint an umber flag on any cluster whose answers share near-duplicate phrasing or a single funding source, and flagged clusters lose attestation weight. Invite growth is limited to one vine per established identity each epoch; if that vine later colludes, the sponsor's locked deposit is slashed, which makes a farm of fake leaves costlier than honest work.
